questions: Does the five-sensor, 2 cm spacing array give a usable, non-saturated signal across the 25 mm tape at the planned speed? Do any sensors sit fully on or off tape for long stretches?
Is the 4 cm forward offset too far ahead, or too close, for the controller to act on without oscillation?
Is there a mismatch between sensor noise and the signal scale that makes the controller hard to tune?
Does the 0.12 m wheel track or 0.7 kg mass limit achievable speed, or cause wheel slip on bends?

intent: Baseline symmetric five-sensor array, 2 cm spacing, 4 cm ahead of the axle, 12 mm footprints, moderate wheel track and light body. Goal: a stable, low-inertia platform that keeps the line inside the array at about 1.5 m/s, so the Integrator has a clean base to tune. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, possibly on the slalom, with few line-loss events. If line loss or large rms_error appears, the next change will widen the array or move it forward.
learning: No race evidence yet. Next iteration should test whether the array width and forward offset hold the line through the slalom, and whether the 0.7 kg mass and 0.12 m track are the right trade-off between speed and turn authority.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no integration feedback, so this is a baseline geometry built from the contract's physics, not from evidence. Finishing in under 3 s needs about 1.5 m/s average speed, so the platform must be stable at speed. A five-sensor array spaced 2 cm apart across ±4 cm gives a usable reading width for a 25 mm tape, so the line stays inside the array through bends. Sensors sit 4 cm ahead of the axle so the signal reacts before the wheels reach a bend. The 12 mm footprint covers roughly half the tape width, so readings change smoothly as the line moves across. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give moderate turn authority without excessive yaw inertia. Mass 0.7 kg with a 0.16 m body keeps inertia low for quick corrections. The off-track limit works out to max(0.06, 0.0125+0.03)=0.06 m, which is a comfortable margin beyond the sensor array. I expect this baseline to complete the oval and s-bend, with the slalom as the hardest case, and I expect line-loss events to be the first sign of a geometry problem if the array is too narrow or too far forward.
